title: Decorated names
description:
Work out the names the 32-bit compiler gives `extern "C"` functions for each calling convention.

```
int __cdecl add(int, int)            -> _add
int __stdcall add(int, int)          -> _add@8
int __fastcall add(int, int)         -> @add@8
void __stdcall init(void)            -> _init@0
double __stdcall scale(double, int)  -> _scale@12
```
hints: `(size + 3) / 4 * 4` rounds each argument up to 4 bytes (lesson 2.02).
`cdecl` adds only the underscore; `fastcall` starts with `@` instead.
requirements: The number after `@` is the bytes of arguments, each rounded up to 4.
Note in a comment that 64-bit Windows has one convention and does not decorate C names.
stretch: Explain why a `.def` file is often used to export `_add@8` simply as `add`.
